text:
alex: Quick async check — we're about to land the change that adds `usage.cached_tokens` to the inference response. Wanted to confirm expected accounting semantics before the PR.

sophia: quick question — is `cached_tokens` additive to prompt/completion counts or is it a separate breakdown that shouldn't contribute to billed total? :thinking_face:

devin: intent was to expose cached tokens as a separate metric (visibility only). billing_total should still be computed from prompt+completion only. we don't want cached tokens double-counted.

liam: +1 to separate visibility. but we need a clear definition in the API contract, otherwise contract consumers might interpret `total_tokens` differently.

maria: what about clients that rely on `total_tokens` for per-request charge? if we keep `total_tokens = prompt+completion` and add `cached_tokens` separately, downstream analytics will be fine. but we need to avoid ambiguous field names.

alex: proposed response shape in PR: 
```json
{
  "id": "req_...",
  "model": "redwood-3b",
  "choices": [...],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 120,
    "completion_tokens": 30,
    "total_tokens": 150,
    "cached_tokens": 40  // tokens served from KV/prefix cache (visibility only)
  }
}
```
This keeps `total_tokens == prompt+completion`. `cached_tokens` is orthogonal.

emma-accounting: Confirming accounting rules: billed units = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens. Cached tokens are measurement-only and should not be billed. If you ship this shape we can update billing docs and reconciliation.

sophia: two follow-ups: 1) how do we report when cached prefix reduces prompt tokens (i.e., prompt_tokens already reflect cache savings, right?) 2) what about streaming where completion is produced in chunks and cache is partially used mid-stream — how is cached_tokens counted?

devin: good call. design notes: prompt_tokens should be the actual tokens consumed on compute (after cache hits applied). So if cache avoided 20 prompt tokens, prompt_tokens will be 100 not 120. `cached_tokens` should report the *number of tokens satisfied by cache* for visibility (20 in that example). For streaming, we increment `cached_tokens` as cache hits occur during generation. On finalization we compute prompt_tokens + completion_tokens based on what actually ran on the GPU.

liam: need to ensure `total_tokens` remains stable for backwards compat. Some customers use `total_tokens` for billing reconciliation. So we should avoid changing semantics: keep `total_tokens = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens`.

maria: PLG metric teams also rely on aggregate totals. Emma, can accounting adapt existing ingestion to ignore `cached_tokens` if present?

emma-accounting: yes, ingestion will continue using prompt+completion. We'll add a new column `cached_tokens` in reporting for visibility. We'll also add a reconciliation flag to detect if any client still attempts to sum `cached_tokens` into billed totals — we can surface anomalies.

alex: devops note: adding `cached_tokens` to the response is a non-breaking additive change. But one compatibility risk: some SDKs de-serialize `usage` into strict structs and may fail on unknown fields. We should be explicit in the SDK changelogs and bump minor versions.

sophia: good point. we'll include a compatibility guide in the PR description: recommend tolerant parsing, link to SDK updates.

devin: impl detail for runtime: kernel-level accounting will track two counters: tokens_computed and tokens_served_from_cache. We'll populate usage accordingly at end of request. For streaming we flush partial usage at end only (so no mid-stream usage events), because we can't reliably expose final numbers until request completes. But that means streaming clients won't see interim counts — ok?

maria: hmm, some observability dashboards expect streaming partial `usage` in evented form. Are we ok postponing until end?

alex: plan: initial rollout end-only usage, then follow-up RFC for streaming partial telemetry (event webhooks). Keep the API response stable.

liam: PR link? ping for review pls.

alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4523 — draft up, tests added. devin and sophia can you review? :pray:

devin: on it. small nit: in tests use `assert usage.get('total_tokens') == usage['prompt_tokens'] + usage['completion_tokens']` to avoid regressions.

emma-accounting: also adding a small note: when customers are on Dedicated with custom billing hooks, cached tokens might be billable per contract. We should allow an org-level flag `billing.include_cached_tokens: true|false` in future, but default false. I'll open a ticket for contract exceptions.

sophia: noted. add a chord to the PR description: "org override for billing semantics" and link accounting ticket.

alex: thanks all. action items: 1) devin/sophia review PR, 2) alex to update docs + changelog, 3) emma to update billing ingestion and open contract-exception ticket, 4) liaise with SDK owners for minor bump. I'll merge after approvals.

billing-bot: [billing ingestion job scheduled — schema update `cached_tokens` -> downstream column created] :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — will update PLG dashboards after merged. :rocket:
